papers.title: The accessory protein ORF3a hijacks the CLCC1 chloride channel to disrupt ER homeostasis in betacoronavirus pathogenesis.
papers.summary: SARS-CoV-2 ORF3a binds the ER chloride channel CLCC1, disrupting ER ion homeostasis, activating the unfolded protein response and ER-phagy. CLCC1 counteracts ORF3a by retaining it in the ER, acting as a restriction factor; ORF3a later escapes to lysosomes. This conserved betacoronavirus strategy recapitulates COVID-19 neurological features in mouse brain.

papers.title: ENPP1 buffers extracellular cGAMP in brown adipose tissue to limit insulin resistance.
papers.summary: Using a cGAMP-hydrolysis-deficient Enpp1 mouse, loss of ENPP1 cGAMP clearance worsened high-fat-diet weight gain and insulin resistance. Mitochondrial DNA leakage in brown adipocytes drives extracellular cGAMP, which suppresses glucose uptake via STING and polarizes macrophages. A human obesity-associated ENPP1 variant shows reduced hydrolysis.

papers.title: Sex-ratio distorters enable pre-zygotic sexing for sex-specific transcriptomics in Anopheles gambiae embryos.
papers.summary: Synthetic X- and Y-shredder sex-ratio distorters enabled pre-zygotic sexing of Anopheles gambiae embryos, generating male- or female-biased cohorts for long- and short-read RNA-seq. The resulting sex-specific transcriptomic dataset identified four sex-specific spliced genes linked to the sex-determination network, informing mosquito biology and vector-control strategies.

papers.title: Engineered bacterial outer membrane vesicle vaccine prevents T cell exhaustion for antibacterial immunotherapy.
papers.summary: Porphyrin-mediated metal-ion nanoshells engineered onto Porphyromonas gingivalis outer membrane vesicles promote dendritic-cell uptake, lysosomal escape, and cytosolic cross-presentation via STING, while dampening endotoxin-driven cytokine storms. In murine periodontitis the vaccine reduced bacterial burden, prevented T cell exhaustion, and lessened tissue damage.

papers.title: Perifusate metabolomics interrogates nutrient exposure and oxidative stress response in kidney tubules.
papers.summary: A perifusion platform enabled >45,000 time-resolved metabolite measurements across living kidney tubule and glomerulus preparations. Tubules released TCA-cycle and acetylated amino-acid intermediates and showed sex-dependent antioxidative and urea-cycle responses to amino acid exposure; stress-released metabolites matched plasma signatures in acute kidney injury patients.

papers.title: The RAMP3 proximity interactor MYO6 determines spatiotemporal signaling of the GPCR CLR in lymphatic endothelial cells.
papers.summary: Proximity proteomics identified the motor MYO6 as a RAMP3–calcitonin receptor-like receptor interactor. In primary lymphatic endothelial cells, MYO6 knockdown blunted adrenomedullin-stimulated Gαs/ERK/AKT signaling while raising cAMP-PKA-CREB activity, and blocked receptor internalization into Rab5 endosomes, altering junction remodeling and migration.

papers.title: Viral hijacking of the host ubiquitin-proteasome system for immune escape.
papers.summary: This Science Signalling highlight summarizes Glassman et al. (Science, 20 Aug 2026): viral proteins commandeer the host ubiquitin-proteasome system—including E3 ligase-mediated degradative and nondegradative ubiquitylation—to dysregulate innate immunity and escape antiviral responses, revealing potential targets for antiviral intervention.

papers.title: Bi-allelic GAD2 variants cause a rare developmental encephalopathy with early-onset seizures.
papers.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
papers.summary: Four individuals from three families carried bi-allelic GAD2 loss-of-function variants causing early-onset epilepsy, developmental delay, intellectual disability, and autism. A Gad65 knockout mouse reproduced spontaneous seizures, behavioral abnormalities, and dysregulated metabolic and mitochondrial pathways, establishing GAD2 as a recessive encephalopathy gene.

papers.title: Spire1 and active INF2 promote ER-mitochondria contacts to enhance mitochondrial fission factor-mediated mitochondrial fission.
papers.summary: In MCF-7 cells, Spire1 together with activated INF2 increases ER-mitochondria contacts and mitochondrial fission events while shortening fission duration; MFF knockout abolishes these effects, placing MFF downstream. FRET analysis suggests Spire1 and INF2 tighten MFF oligomers, promoting MFF-mediated mitochondrial fission.

papers.title: Phosphorylation of BigH1 regulates its expression pattern and promotes embryonic development.
papers.summary: In Drosophila, the germline linker histone BigH1 is replaced by H1 during early embryogenesis. Loss of N-terminal phosphorylation prevented BigH1 clearance from somatic nuclei, while disrupting C-terminal phosphorylation impaired early nuclear divisions and compromised embryonic development, showing domain-specific phosphorylation coordinates BigH1 turnover.

papers.title: iKa/Ks: Estimating the Selection Pressure and Evolutionary Rate of Proteins under the Non-neutral Hypothesis of Synonymous Mutations.
papers.summary: iKa/Ks redefines the neutral substitution rate by incorporating synonymous mutations' functional effects on miRNA regulation. The improved metric correlates better with human–mouse expression distance than conventional Ka/Ks and uncovers selected genes missed previously (e.g., TMEM72 scored positively selected where Ka/Ks called it negatively selected).

papers.title: The Cancer Noise Atlas (TCNA): A Webserver of Multiscale Transcriptional Noise in Cancer.
papers.summary: The Cancer Noise Atlas is a webserver quantifying transcriptional noise from TCGA/GDC bulk RNA-seq at gene, pathway, and tumor scales using metrics including CV, SD, MAD, and DEPTH/DEPTH2. It catalogs tumor expression heterogeneity to support studies of disease progression and therapeutic response.

papers.title: ShapeME: A Tool and Web Front-end for De Novo Discovery of Structural Motifs Underpinning Protein-DNA Interactions.
papers.summary: ShapeME is a workflow and web front-end that discovers DNA structural motifs (e.g., narrow minor groove) from virtually any sequence-coverage or enrichment data (ChIP-seq, SELEX, RNA-seq). Applied to ENCODE datasets, it identifies proteins for which short structural motifs outperform the best JASPAR PWM or STREME sequence motif.

papers.title: GalaxyCDock: Webserver for Covalent Protein-Ligand Binding Mode Prediction.
papers.summary: GalaxyCDock is a webserver predicting covalent protein–ligand binding modes by combining GalaxyDock2 pose sampling with a deep-learning score. It outperformed AutoDock4 and Dock6, achieving up to 80% re-docking and 61% cross-docking success, and offers a practical alternative to AlphaFold3/Boltz-2 when receptor structures are available.

papers.title: plantiSMASH 2.0: Improvements to Detection, Annotation, and Prioritization of Plant Biosynthetic Gene Clusters.
papers.summary: plantiSMASH 2.0 expands rule-based detection of plant biosynthetic gene clusters to 12 BGC types, adds substrate prediction for selected enzyme families and transcription-factor binding site regulatory analysis, and ships a database of 30,423 putative BGCs across 430 genomes, accelerating plant natural-product discovery.

papers.title: IMDD: A Database for Exploring Tissue-Specific Gene Expression Dynamics During Holometabolous Insects.
papers.summary: IMDD integrates >1,200 bulk-tissue transcriptomes and >1.4 million single-cell profiles for four holometabolous insects (Drosophila, Bombyx, Aedes, Apis), enabling tissue- and single-cell-resolution exploration of metamorphic gene expression dynamics, cellular heterogeneity, and cell-type transitions across developmental stages.

papers.title: NMRhub: An NMR Data Ecosystem Spanning the Complete Data Lifecycle.
papers.summary: NMRhub links the NSF Network for Advanced NMR, NMRbox, and BMRB into an ecosystem spanning the complete NMR data lifecycle—from automated instrument harvest and metadata parsing to virtualized processing environments and curated archival—with single sign-on and machine-learning-enhanced search supporting reproducibility and meta-analysis.

papers.title: Paean: A Unified and Efficient Transcriptome Quantification System Using Heterogeneous Computing.
papers.summary: Paean is a GPU-CPU parallel system unifying gene-expression and alternative-splicing quantification. It matches existing precision while running >100-fold faster with fewer resources, quantifying all 10,866 TCGA samples in ~3,400 minutes and enabling rapid identification of tumor neoantigen candidates from RNA splicing events.

papers.title: STEGG: Structural TCR-pMHC ensemble generator and gallery.
papers.summary: STEGG generates structural ensembles of TCR–pMHC complexes from sequence, capturing flexible CDR-loop and peptide conformations through domain-specific sampling rather than costly molecular dynamics. It recovers low-RMSD conformations to experimental structures and provides a public database and webserver of predicted ensembles.

papers.title: GLASS2: An Updated Database for Comprehensive Experimentally Validated GPCR-ligand Associations.
papers.summary: GLASS2 expands GPCR-ligand associations 72% over its predecessor by integrating pharmacological databases with LLM-powered PubMed text mining: 1,715 receptors, 450,736 ligands, and >1 million unique interactions. It provides task-ready classification and regression datasets supporting AI-driven GPCR drug discovery.

papers.title: FDB&FragLinker: A Large Fragment Database for Rapid Ligand Optimization Within Protein-Ligand Complex.
papers.summary: FDB&FragLinker couples a fragment database spanning DrugBank and an 800-million-molecule ZINC subset with the first fragment-level 3D complex generation tool. Covalent docking attaches selected fragments onto ligands at defined atoms, yielding higher structural fidelity than traditional docking and faster than diffusion-based generative models.

papers.title: MPKaDB: A pK(a)database for exploring pH dependence in membrane proteins.
papers.summary: MPKaDB is a database decoding protonation states of ionizable residues in membrane proteins at specified pH, providing residue-specific pKa values, cytoplasmic/extracytoplasmic isoelectric points, and automated active-site screening, plus case studies illustrating pH-dependent structure–function relationships in transmembrane proteins.

papers.title: Cell Lines CoCoPUTs: A Database of Codon and Codon-pair Usage Frequencies in Cell Lines.
papers.summary: Cell Lines CoCoPUTs provides transcriptomic-weighted codon and codon-pair usage tables for 1,866 cell lines from COSMIC, CCLE, and the Human Protein Atlas. Unsupervised clustering shows codon-pair usage distinguishes cell lines more sharply, while codon usage tracks tissue of origin more closely than disease phenotype.

papers.title: CLISGen: A Comprehensive Resource of SNP Genotypes for Human Cell Lines.
papers.summary: CLISGen harmonizes whole-genome, whole-exome, and RNA-seq data into SNP genotypes for >1,000 CCLE cancer cell lines, enriched with copy-number alterations and genetic ancestry. Its web application supports variant-, gene-, and region-level searches filtered by tissue and data quality, easing cell-model selection.

papers.title: CHARMM-GUI Quick Bilayer: Simple and Intuitive One-Stop Membrane Bilayer Builder.
papers.summary: CHARMM-GUI Quick Bilayer is a new module providing a streamlined one-stop builder for assembling proteins into biologically relevant lipid bilayers with customizable compositions and lipid search. It adds a REST-like API and command-line interface enabling automated, large-scale membrane simulation system generation.

papers.title: VarXOmics: A Versatile Web Server for Genomic Data Querying, Analysis, and Variant Prioritization With Multi-omics Insights.
papers.summary: VarXOmics is an end-to-end web server for querying variants and genes, streamlining germline variant analysis, and prioritizing variants with multi-omics evidence. Analyzing a breast cancer WGS case, it prioritized BRCA2 c.3751dup as pathogenic and highlighted cell-cycle, DNA-repair, and type 2 diabetes associations via enrichment and network analysis.

papers.title: Alpha&ESMhFolds: An Updated Web Server for the Comparison, Evaluation, and Annotation of Human AlphaFold2 and ESMFold Models.
papers.summary: Alpha&ESMhFolds updates a public database pairing human AlphaFold2 and ESMFold models against UniProt 2025_04, adding Pfam functional mapping and external quality metrics. Both methods converge with high pLDDT in Pfam-covered regions regardless of overall model quality, helping users select better models for downstream analysis.

papers.title: ProteoCast: a web server to predict, validate, and interpret missense variant effects.
papers.summary: ProteoCast predicts missense variant effects via evolutionary constraint and structural context, classifying variants as impactful, mild, or neutral with MSA quality controls. On 63,000 ClinVar variants it showed 77% sensitivity and 87% specificity, and it identifies functional linear peptides in disordered regions better than conservation methods.

papers.title: ModelCIF Update: Supporting Emerging Classes of Computational Macromolecular Models.
papers.summary: The ModelCIF data standard extension supports emerging computational modeling use cases beyond homology/ab initio protein prediction: protein–ligand and protein–protein interactions, multiple conformational states, and de novo protein design. New guidelines capture protocols, inputs, and outputs to promote reproducibility, validation, and FAIR reuse of models.

papers.title: HMRPred: A Machine Learning-Based Web Resource for Identification of Heavy Metal Resistance Proteins.
papers.summary: HMRPred is a machine-learning web resource classifying heavy metal resistance proteins across ten metals (arsenic through zinc), trained on experimentally validated datasets with sequence-derived features. It achieved >98% AUC-ROC in cross-validation and independent testing, supporting genome-wide annotation for bioremediation and synthetic biology.

papers.title: DynaBench: Dynamic data for the docking benchmark.
papers.summary: DynaBench provides molecular dynamics simulation data (three 100 ns replicas each) for over 200 protein–protein complexes from Docking Benchmark 5.5, capturing interface dynamics absent from static AlphaFold/docking models. Publicly available trajectories support ML training, model-evaluation metrics, and protein interface design.

papers.title: ProHistoneDB: A database of prokaryotic and viral histones.
papers.summary: ProHistoneDB catalogs 7,334 prokaryotic and viral histones grouped into 24 categories by predicted multimerization state (monomer through hexamer), reflecting diverse DNA-bending and -bridging modes. It provides structure predictions, interactive phylogenetic trees, and HMM profile logos for exploring histone evolution and conserved residues.

papers.title: AggrescanAI: Prediction of Aggregation-Prone Regions Using Contextualized Embeddings.
papers.summary: AggrescanAI predicts residue-level aggregation-prone regions directly from sequence using ProtT5 protein language model embeddings, trained on experimentally annotated APRs expanded by homology. It outperforms state-of-the-art predictors, captures aggregation shifts from pathogenic mutations, and is offered via an open Google Colab notebook.

papers.title: TLSEA 2.0: an updated tool for lncRNA enrichment analysis.
papers.summary: TLSEA 2.0 expands lncRNA enrichment analysis with tripled reference lncRNA sets and five analysis categories: disease, drug, RNA–RNA interaction, RNA–protein interaction, and cancer phenotype. It adds similarity-network-based list expansion and replaces traditional graph representation learning with combined graph attention and convolutional networks.

papers.title: PDBe-KB Complexes: Enabling Functional Insight from Macromolecular Complexes in the PDB.
papers.summary: PDBe-KB Complexes aggregates experimentally determined PDB assemblies into >100,000 unique complex-level records unifying stoichiometry, symmetry, ligands, and assembly properties. Demonstrated on the SARS-CoV-2 spike, it reveals conformational diversity and antibody binding beyond single PDB entries, supporting comparative functional analysis.

papers.title: IHMValidation: Assessment of Integrative Structure Models Deposited to the Protein Data Bank.
papers.summary: IHMValidation is a pipeline assessing integrative/hybrid structure models deposited in PDB-IHM (374 entries as of October 2025). It generates PDF/HTML reports covering data quality, local geometry, and model fit to both modeling and validation data, following wwPDB task force plus SAS, crosslinking-MS, and 3DEM community recommendations.

papers.title: Missense3D-PTMdb: A Web Tool for Visualising and Exploring Human Genetic Variants and Post-translational Modification Sites Using AlphaFold Models.
papers.summary: Missense3D-PTMdb maps >11.5 million human missense variants, >60 PTM types, and 203,775 PTM residues onto AlphaFold models of 20,235 human proteins, flagging substitutions that may disrupt post-translational modification sites in sequence and 3D structure. It also supports visualization of user-supplied novel variants.

papers.title: RNAsolo 2.0: multimodal database to study RNAs, their structural families and intermolecular interfaces.
papers.summary: RNAsolo 2.0 adds Rfam-based family classification, >2,500 precompiled benchmark sets, and multimodal representations (sequence, secondary/tertiary structure, torsion angles) to its cleaned, non-redundant RNA 3D structure database. It enables searching RNAs interacting with specific proteins, ligands, or ions with interactive interface views for AI-driven modeling.

papers.title: gutSMASH 2.0: Extended Identification of Primary Metabolic Gene Clusters From the Human Gut Microbiota.
papers.summary: gutSMASH 2.0 expands detection of primary metabolic gene clusters in anaerobic gut microbes with 14 new rules covering 12 additional MGC types, an enhanced comparative genomics framework built on 26 validated MGCs and 15,024 CGR2 clusters, and transcription factor binding site prediction for MGC regulatory analysis.

papers.title: Dockground: Expanding the Resource to Protein-DNA Complexes.
papers.summary: Dockground expands its macromolecular interaction resource to protein–DNA complexes, adding automatic weekly updates and a user-friendly search, analysis, and download interface alongside existing protein–protein and protein–RNA data. Utility is illustrated by benchmarking AlphaFold3 predictions on protein–DNA complexes.

papers.title: GnRH Promotes Gonadotropin Synthesis and Secretion in the Bovine Anterior Pituitary by Inhibiting METTL1-Mediated m7G Modification of FOXO1 mRNA.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: In bovine pituitary cells, GnRH promoted gonadotropin synthesis/secretion while reducing global m7G methylation and downregulating METTL1. METTL1 methylates FOXO1 mRNA (m7G), modulating its stability and protein expression as a negative regulator of gonadotropin release, revealing RNA epigenetic control of bovine reproduction.

papers.title: Therapeutic Potential of Linalool in Endometriosis: Modulation of Oxidative Stress, Inflammation, and Apoptosis in a Rat Model.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: In a rat endometriosis model, 28-day linalool treatment (50–100 mg/kg) reduced lesion size and oxidative stress dose-dependently, with near-normal histology at the high dose. It boosted antioxidant enzymes, suppressed NF-κB/MAPK inflammatory signaling, promoted apoptosis, and reduced angiogenesis and cellular adhesion.

papers.title: Integrative Transcriptomic Profiling Delineates LTBP4-Driven Fibroblast Reprogramming Across the Ossification Continuum of the Ligamentum Flavum.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: RNA-seq across normal, immature, and mature ossification of the ligamentum flavum identified progressive LTBP4 downregulation (AUC 0.88), localized to fibroblasts by single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. Virtual LTBP4 knockout in fibroblasts recapitulated the OLF signature, and AI-based screening nominated stage-specific drug candidates including BRD-K59831625.

papers.title: Stressor- and Tissue-Specific Regulation of the Corticotropin-Releasing Factor System Across Epithelial Tissues in Rainbow Trout.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Characterizing the corticotropin-releasing factor system in rainbow trout gills and intestine, vaccination altered intestinal CRF transcripts without gill effects, whereas seawater transfer increased mid-intestine transcripts and reduced gill binding proteins/receptors. Feeding state shifted intestinal CRF transcripts region-specifically, indicating tissue- and stressor-specific peripheral roles.

papers.title: Purinergic Receptor P2Y2 Regulates Neurogenesis and Functional Recovery Following Spinal Cord Injury in Zebrafish.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: In adult zebrafish spinal cord injury, the purinergic receptor P2Y2 was dysregulated and its pharmacological inhibition reduced swim capacity. P2Y2 was expressed on proliferating ependymal radial glial cells, but inhibition spared their proliferation while attenuating neurogenesis, indicating a pro-neurogenic role supporting functional recovery.

papers.title: Sarsasapogenin Preserves Podocyte Integrity and Attenuates Renal Injury in Experimental IgA Nephropathy.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: In rat IgA nephropathy, sarsasapogenin (60 mg/kg/day, weeks 7–12) reduced proteinuria and improved renal function, decreasing IL-6 inflammation and TGF-β1/Smad3 activation while preserving nephrin, podocin, and podocyte ultrastructure and lowering pre-fibrotic markers, supporting further study as an early-stage IGAN therapy.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Genome-Wide to Explore the Formation and Development Targets for Intracranial Aneurysms.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Integrating ISGC and UK Biobank data with mediation analysis, virtual knockouts, and phenome-wide Mendelian randomization, this study identified drug targets for intracranial aneurysms—five for IAS formation including FKTN, MAP3K1, PSMA4, SLC22A4, ADAM17—with SLC22A4 showing expression in blood and brain and no adverse phenome-wide associations.

papers.title: Investigating Dietary microRNA Stability and Function Using a Transgenic Milk Model With Unique microRNA Sequences.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Using transgenic cows expressing four unique milk microRNAs (amirs), this study confirmed amir association with milk extracellular vesicles and differential resistance to simulated digestion, but found no significant regulatory effect in Caco-2 cells exposed to milk EVs, suggesting absent or non-functional uptake in this in vitro model.

papers.title: PEBP1 Regulates Ferroptosis in Acute Glaucoma: Targeted Therapy Using Engineered Exosomes.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of rat glaucoma identified PEBP1 upregulation in injured retinal ganglion cells tracking ferroptosis activation. AAV-mediated knockdown suppressed ferroptosis via GPX4/ACSL4 and preserved vision, while engineered mesenchymal exosomes carrying siPEBP1 enabled immediate single-dose protection, outperforming AAV in the acute window.

papers.title: Bile Acid Metabolism as a Unifying Readout for Diet, Microbiome Function, and Gastrointestinal Disease.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: This perspective argues bile acid biology–medicine gap persists because research isn't organized around the bile acid pool as a shared measurable output. With microbially conjugated bile acids discovered in 2020 and >200 species cataloged, it recommends routine bile acid outcome measurement, clinical testing, regulatory frameworks, and population-scale monitoring infrastructure.

papers.title: ASIV Attenuates Cisplatin-Induced Proximal Tubular Injury by Enhancing Mitochondrial Biogenesis and Mitophagy Through the ADRA1A/AMPK/FOXO3A Pathway.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Astragaloside IV (ASIV) protected against cisplatin-induced proximal tubular injury by upregulating ADRA1A, activating AMPK/FOXO3A phosphorylation, and enhancing mitochondrial biogenesis and mitophagy (PGC-1α, TOMM20, PINK1). The ADRA1A agonist dabuzalgron recapitulated protection; tamsulosin or ADRA1A siRNA abrogated it.

papers.title: Annexin A4 Deficient Ventricular Myocytes Display Advanced Hypertrophy and Electrical Remodeling With Chronic β-Adrenoceptor Stimulation.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Annexin A4, a negative AC5 modulator, was examined in gene-trap deficient mice under chronic isoprenaline. A4-deficient myocytes showed advanced hypertrophy, prolonged action potentials, reduced Ito, and enhanced AC/cAMP/PKA signaling with preserved acute cAMP response, supporting Annexin A4 peptide as a candidate antiremodeling therapeutic.

papers.title: Sesamin Promotes Diabetic Wound Healing by Inhibiting Ferroptosis via the SIRT1/Keap1/Nrf2 Pathway.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Sesamin promoted diabetic wound healing in streptozotocin mice by activating SIRT1, promoting KEAP1/NRF2 dissociation and NRF2 nuclear translocation, thereby upregulating anti-ferroptosis proteins including GPX4. In HUVECs under high glucose, sesamin dose-dependently suppressed ferroptosis; SIRT1 knockdown abrogated all protective effects.

papers.title: Transcriptomic and Metabolomic Profiling Identifies a Core Gene-Metabolite Axis Driving African Swine Fever Virus Replication in the Soft Tick Ornithodoros lahorensis.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Integrating transcriptomics and metabolomics of African swine fever virus infection in the soft tick Ornithodoros lahorensis across three stages revealed a conserved module of 12 core genes and 8 metabolites supporting viral replication. siRNA silencing of TK1, ATP5F1B, or IMPDH suppressed ASFV loads by 87.8–91.5%.

papers.title: Superantigens in Cancer Immunotherapy: Mechanisms, Engineering Strategies, and Therapeutic Potential.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: This review describes how bacterial superantigens—binding MHC-II and TCR Vβ simultaneously to activate large T-cell populations—can be engineered into cancer immunotherapy platforms. Low-toxicity variants, antibody fusions, nanoparticles, and tumor-targeted constructs aim to improve specificity and synergize with checkpoint blockade and adoptive cell therapies.

papers.title: Evaluating the Validity of Model Organisms: A Review and a New Framework for Biologists.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: This conceptual analysis reviews philosophical arguments for generalizing knowledge from model organisms and proposes a new framework of criteria for assessing their external validity toward other species or human clinical contexts, designed for practical use by biologists evaluating non-traditional emerging models.

papers.title: An Integrated Proteomics and Genomics Approach to Identify Essential Protein Kinases During Human Trophoblast Development.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Using human trophoblast stem cells with quantitative proteomics and phosphoproteomics, this study identified kinases maintaining stem state (BUB1B, PAK6, PKMYT1, TNIK), atypical PKCζ for syncytiotrophoblast development, and PTK2B, SRC, TRIO, LYN for extravillous trophoblast development—kinases whose inhibition could impair placentation.

papers.title: d-Sorbose Promotes Regulatory T-Cell Differentiation and Ameliorates Autoimmune and Allergic Diseases via Hexosamine Biosynthetic Pathway Inhibition.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: d-Sorbose, the C-3 epimer of D-fructose, increased Foxp3+ regulatory T-cell frequencies comparably to D-mannose without reducing CD8+ T cells. In vivo it ameliorated airway inflammation and autoimmune diabetes, promoting IL-10-producing Tregs through coordinated glucose partitioning and glutamine catabolism with favorable long-term safety.

papers.title: Differential Transcriptomic and Adhesion Responses of Human Periodontal Ligament Cells to Cyclic and Static Hydrostatic Pressure.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Comparing static versus cyclic hydrostatic pressure in human periodontal ligament cells, cyclic pressure induced broader transcriptional remodeling, selectively upregulating focal adhesion genes (ILK, PXN, TNS1, FHL3, YWHAZ) while downregulating integrins ITGA4/ITGB8. ILK silencing attenuated pressure-induced AKT activation and focal adhesion formation.

papers.title: Nucleic Acids as Emerging Regulators of Calcium Phosphate Biomineralization.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: This review assembles evidence that nucleic acids—via their phosphate backbone, structural versatility, and calcium phosphate interactions—adsorb, coprecipitate, and template mineral formation. It discusses extracellular nucleic acids in mineralized and ectopically mineralizing tissues from bacteria, EVs, cell death, and NETs, proposing mechanistic model refinement.

papers.title: METTL18 is Required for Developmental, Metabolic, and Endocrine Regulation of Mammalian Growth.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Mettl18 knockout mice show impaired embryonic growth with disrupted transferrin–transferrin receptor iron handling, postnatal underweight, reduced liver and adipose mass, decreased triglycerides with improved glucose tolerance, and impaired IGF-1 signaling and TSH–T4 axis, establishing histidine methylation as required for mammalian growth regulation.

papers.title: Outer membrane proteins mediate unconventional secretion of Pseudomonas peroxidase through crosstalk between the Sec pathway and outer membrane vesicles.
papers.summary: In Pseudomonas putida, the Sec-translocated lipoprotein LPP1528 recognizes the C-terminal hydrophobic region of signal-peptide-lacking peroxidase DypB2985 for inner membrane translocation, then OmpW4836 mediates its incorporation into outer membrane vesicles for secretion—stepwise crosstalk with biotechnological OMV functionalization potential.

papers.title: Early glucagon-positive cells restrict pancreatic branching through VMAT2-noradrenaline-mediated ROS signaling.
papers.summary: In pancreatic bud explants, inhibiting VMAT2-mediated catecholamine uptake increased epithelial branching and insulin-expressing cells. Early glucagon/insulin co-expressing cells signal via VMAT2–noradrenaline–ROS; lineage-specific Vmat2 deletion in glucagon cells increased branching and islet areas while decreasing ROS accumulation.

papers.title: METTL7B attenuates pathological cardiac hypertrophy via m6A-associated regulation of HK3.
papers.summary: Integrating RNA-seq and MeRIP-seq of human hypertrophic/failing hearts, METTL7B and HK3 showed coordinated downregulation with reduced HK3 m6A. METTL7B or HK3 overexpression attenuated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy in vitro and TAC-induced remodeling in vivo, with YTHDC1 identified as an HK3 RNA-associated factor stabilizing HK3 mRNA.

papers.title: Dapagliflozin attenuates methotrexate-induced hepatorenal toxicity in rats: insights into oxidative stress, inflammation, autophagy and apoptosis.
papers.summary: In rats, dapagliflozin (10 mg/kg, 10 days) ameliorated methotrexate-induced hepatorenal toxicity, upregulating PPAR-γ/NRF-2/HO-1 while suppressing NF-κB, restoring GSH/MDA oxidative balance, and modulating Beclin1/LC3 autophagy and caspase-3/Bcl-2 apoptosis in hepatic and renal tissues.

papers.title: Benzo[a]pyrene-derived quinones exploit mitochondrial electron transport to drive catalytic redox cycling and potent ROS amplification.
papers.summary: Benzo[a]pyrene-derived quinones undergo redox cycling in isolated mitochondria, stimulating KCN-resistant oxygen consumption and producing superoxide and hydrogen peroxide—with BP-1,6-quinone active at submicromolar levels. Complexes I and III are the principal electron transport chain sites supporting this ROS amplification mechanism.

papers.title: Vitamin B6 attenuates diabetic cardiomyopathy by targeting CtBP1 and alleviating Golgi stress via the AKT/HO-1 signaling pathway.
papers.summary: In a high-fat diet/streptozotocin mouse model of diabetic cardiomyopathy, vitamin B6 improved cardiac function and reduced fibrosis, restoring CtBP1, GM130, HO-1, and p-AKT while lowering NHE1, and ameliorating Golgi fragmentation and mitochondrial damage—implicating CtBP1-linked Golgi stress in diabetic cardiomyopathy.

papers.title: Analysis of motor-based transport in primary cilia by dynamic mode decomposition of live-cell imaging data.
papers.summary: Combining live-cell imaging with dynamic mode decomposition-based kymograph analysis, this study shows a KIF13B motor-domain deletion mutant doesn't alter steady-state intraflagellar transport. However, dynein-2 inhibition by ciliobrevin D or tanespimycin reduced IFT velocities in parental but not KIF13B mutant cells, clarifying KIF13B ciliary roles.

papers.title: Asperulosidic Acid Attenuates Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury and Suppresses MAPK Signaling.
papers.summary: Asperulosidic acid protected against myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury in H9C2 cells and rat LAD ligation models, reducing infarct size, CK/LDH release, inflammatory cytokines, ROS, and apoptosis. Network pharmacology identified MAPK pathway suppression—reduced p38, ERK, and JNK phosphorylation—as the mechanism.

papers.title: Leucine-rich glioma inactivated 1 (LGI1) is a ganglioside-binding protein.
papers.summary: LGI1 contains multiple conserved canonical ganglioside-binding domains; GT1b co-purifies with LGI1 from native rat brain, and recombinant LGI1 binds ganglioside-containing liposomes. The authors propose LG1 organizes lipid membrane platforms accommodating protein complexes, whose loss destabilizes Kv1 channel expression in LGI1-deficient mice.

papers.title: L-aspartate oxidase provides new insights into fumarate reduction in anaerobic darkness in Synechocystis sp. PCC6803.
papers.summary: In Synechocystis PCC6803, succinate dehydrogenase deletion strains accumulated more succinate during dark anaerobic fermentation, indicating SDH acts oxidatively rather than reducing fumarate. Purified L-aspartate oxidase instead showed L-aspartate–fumarate oxidoreductase activity generating succinate, clarifying anaerobic succinate formation routes.

papers.title: Bacterial RNA downregulates MHC-I in tumor cell lines, promoting NK response and delaying tumor growth.
papers.summary: Brucella abortus RNA (bacRNA) diminished IFN-γ-induced MHC-I surface expression across human glioblastoma, colorectal, breast, and murine melanoma cell lines via TLR8 (mimicked by hTLR8 agonist ORN06). Reduced MHC-I increased NK cytotoxicity, enhanced immune infiltration, and delayed B16 melanoma growth, proposing a therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Computational prediction of a multi-epitope Human Metapneumovirus vaccine candidate through integrated reverse vaccinology and pan-genomic approaches.
papers.summary: Using reverse vaccinology and pan-genomics across 65 global Human Metapneumovirus sequences, this computational study prioritized 15 conserved MHC-I, MHC-II, and B-cell epitopes into three constructs. Lead candidate HMPV-V2 showed excellent structural quality, strong predicted TLR4 binding, and robust simulated adaptive responses—entirely computational, lacking experimental validation.

papers.title: Shared genetic basis and spatial cellular atlas of psoriasis and metabolic syndrome.
papers.summary: Integrating GWAS summary statistics for psoriasis and metabolic syndrome with spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomics, this study found significant genetic correlations and polygenic sharing, identified cross-validated shared loci, and revealed tissue-specific enrichment: psoriasis strongest in epidermis, adipose, and liver; waist circumference in adipose.

papers.title: Orchestration of kaempferol nuclear translocation by phase ii metabolic enzymes and efflux transporters suppresses colorectal cancer.
papers.summary: Kaempferol's anti-colorectal cancer efficacy depends on coordinated phase II metabolism and efflux: UGT1A1 knockdown increased nuclear kaempferol exposure but reduced cytotoxicity; BCRP knockdown enhanced efficacy while MDR1 knockdown attenuated it despite raising accumulation. BRG1 was identified as a nuclear target degraded via ubiquitination-proteasome.

papers.title: Patient-specific integration of RNA expression, methylation-derived replication-timing proxies, and histomorphology for pancreatic cancer subtyping.
papers.summary: Integrating RNA expression, methylation-derived replication timing, and histomorphology into patient-specific LIONESS networks for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma subtyping, this study found reproducible gene modules and increased network density with multimodal integration, though individual edge scores didn't improve subtype classification over Moffitt baseline.

papers.title: Hepatitis B virus genome mutations in precore and basal core promoter regions among HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients with high viral load in Indonesia.
papers.summary: In 32 Indonesian chronic hepatitis B patients with high viral load, precore mutations A1846T/C and G1896A were strongly associated with HBeAg-negative status (81.3% vs 6.3% and 75.0% vs 12.5%), explaining HBeAg negativity despite active replication and informing TDF prophylaxis decisions where HBeAg guides eligibility.

papers.title: HMOX2-driven crosstalk between vascular aging and heart failure: A multimodal bioinformatics and explainable machine learning approach with experimental validation.
papers.summary: Integrating heart failure transcriptomics with vascular aging targets and machine learning prioritization identified HMOX2 as the top predictor (AUC 0.978) among 12 core genes, validated by qPCR in doxorubicin-treated vascular smooth muscle and H9C2 cells plus a mouse heart failure model showing cardiac dysfunction, fibrosis, and senescence markers.

papers.title: Comparative phytochemical profiling and bioactivity evaluation of three Indonesian pomegranate (Punica granatum) peel varieties: Antioxidant, antibacterial, and in vitro antiproliferative activities.
papers.summary: Comparing three Indonesian pomegranate peel varieties, ethanolic extracts outperformed n-hexane in phenolic/flavonoid content and antioxidant activity. Purple exocarp showed highest TPC (721 mg GAE/g), TFC (161 mg QE/g), and potency (IC50 <50 μg/ml), with LC-HRMS revealing phenolic acids, flavonoid glycosides, and anthocyanin derivatives.

papers.title: Diversity at the HYP1 locus in potato cyst nematodes does not result from developmentally-programmed somatic mutations.
papers.summary: Testing whether potato cyst nematodes use developmentally-programmed somatic mutation to diversify the parasitism gene HYP1, this study employed long-read sequencing of a simplified genetic system and transgenic yeast to characterize de novo mutations, interpreting findings through population genetic parameters and surrounding genome diversity.

papers.title: Role of Rab4A in the enhancement of cancer cell invasion induced by plasma samples collected during radiotherapy in patients with triple-negative breast cancer.
papers.summary: Radiotherapy plasma from three of six early-stage triple-negative breast cancer patients enhanced TNBC cell invasion versus pre-radiotherapy plasma; two of those patients relapsed. Rab4A knockdown reduced MT1-MMP proteolytic activity and inhibited the invasion increase and metastatic development, suggesting Rab4A targeting to reduce recurrence.

papers.title: Identification of differentially expressed lncRNAs and candidate ceRNA networks across Mastitis stages in Sahiwal cattle.
papers.summary: Characterizing lncRNA profiles and ceRNA networks across healthy, subclinical, and clinical mastitis in Sahiwal cattle, five biologically relevant modules were identified involving urea-cycle/NAD+ metabolism, extracellular antioxidant networks, PTEN/PI3K-AKT signaling, nuclear import machinery, and extracellular matrix remodeling via ADAMTS.

papers.title: Characterization of mesenchymal stromal cell-mediated mitochondrial transfer to healthy and diseased intervertebral disc cells.
papers.summary: Confocal microscopy demonstrated mesenchymal stromal cell mitochondrial transfer to bovine annulus fibrosus cells under healthy and inflammatory conditions, and to diseased patient-derived intervertebral disc cells. Transfer quantity increased under inflammatory stress and with patient age, though functional consequences remain to be determined.

papers.title: Psychometric properties of the Arabic Fear of Happiness Scale in a sample of Lebanese adults.
papers.summary: The Arabic Fear of Happiness Scale, validated in 484 Lebanese adults, showed a one-factor structure with good internal consistency (ω = 0.95), excellent convergent validity (AVE = 0.87), measurement invariance across sexes, and expected correlations with wellbeing, depression, and anxiety—providing a valid tool for Arabic-speaking populations.

papers.title: Improving sport horse selection using machine learning: Early prediction of elite-level show jumping performance.
papers.summary: An XGBoost classifier trained on longitudinal competition records from show jumping horses achieved 83.5% ROC AUC and 80.0% average precision predicting elite (160 cm clear round) performance, outperforming rule-based baselines. SHAP analysis identified obstacle difficulty, performance consistency, and age-related progression as key predictors.

papers.title: Leveraging bioinformatics approaches for drug repositioning in space radiation protection.
papers.summary: Using published murine cardiac proteomic data after simulated galactic cosmic ray exposure, this study built protein–protein interaction networks, mapped drug–protein interactions, and identified 23 unique drug candidates targeting an ATP synthase cluster—providing a hypothesis-generating bioinformatics framework for space radiation countermeasure development.

papers.title: Marker-assisted screening of resistance to fire blight, powdery mildew, and apple scab in local apple varieties from Uzbekistan.
papers.summary: Screening local Uzbek apple varieties with polymorphic DNA markers revealed substantial resistance-gene variation: AE10-375 (fire blight) in 79.8%, PL1/PL2 (powdery mildew) alleles in 75.2%, and VFA2 (apple scab) in 95.4%. Six varieties carried resistance markers for all three diseases, offering donor material for durable breeding programs.

papers.title: Spatial compartmentalization of melanoma cell states reveals CAF-associated tumor cells with enhanced proliferative capacity.
papers.summary: Integrating single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics across 892 regions of interest from primary melanoma, this study found CAF-high regions had significantly lower immune scores with ECM enrichment. Six melanoma cell states emerged, with CAF-associated tumor states showing higher proliferative capacity and correlation with cisplatin sensitivity and trametinib resistance.

papers.title: A biochemical difference between HAI-2 variants causing syndromic and non-syndromic Congenital Sodium Diarrhea.
papers.summary: Comparing HAI-2 variants causing congenital sodium diarrhea, the non-syndromic Y68C variant uniquely failed to inhibit matriptase while all variants showed impaired prostasin inhibition. The authors propose CSD results from uncontrolled proteolytic activity affecting sodium transporters NHE3 and ENaC, suggesting protease inhibitor therapy potential.

papers.title: Sperm subpopulations differing in mitochondrial abundance show divergent nuclear allele frequencies.
papers.summary: Sorting boar sperm by MitoTracker Green fluorescence into low/high mitochondrial subpopulations and whole-genome sequencing revealed 182 candidate SNPs with allele-frequency differences between fractions, suggesting sperm mitochondrial abundance may serve as an indirect, high-throughput marker of nuclear genomic heterogeneity within sires.

papers.title: Nasal exposure to PM2.5 induces testicular injury and activation of pyroptosis-related signaling in rats: Inhibitor intervention and public transcriptomic analysis.
papers.summary: Nasal PM2.5 exposure (10 mg/kg, 4 weeks) induced rat testicular injury and elevated NLRP3, ASC, cleaved caspase-1, cleaved caspase-3, and GSDMD-N, activating pyroptosis-related signaling. Co-treatment with caspase-1 inhibitor Z-YVAD-FMK reduced multiple pyroptosis markers, suggesting PM2.5 testicular toxicity involves NLRP3-mediated pyroptosis.

papers.title: Anticancer activity of asiatic acid in cisplatin-resistant human neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y and its unaffected effect on human neural stem cells.
papers.summary: Asiatic acid (20 μM) combined with cisplatin (2.5 μM) synergistically reduced viability of cisplatin-resistant neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells (CI 0.41) while sparing human neural stem cells. It increased apoptosis, elevated BAX, downregulated BCL2/SOD-1/HO-1, and inhibited GSK3β, supported by molecular docking interactions.

papers.title: Detection of bacterial gene expression elements on Tobacco mosaic virus RNA using cDNA analysis.
papers.summary: Investigating bacterial recognition modules in Tobacco mosaic virus RNA, this study found E. coli ribosomes translate the TMV 5'-UTR and correctly recognize the initiation codon despite an overly long 5'-UTR. cDNA analysis with GFP replacements and promoter prediction revealed an E. coli-specific promoter ~2.1 kb upstream, first revealing bacterial modules within TMV RNA.

papers.title: Esketamine exerts a protective effect against skeletal muscle injury induced by hindlimb ischemia-reperfusion in mice by regulating autophagy.
papers.summary: Esketamine attenuated skeletal muscle injury after hindlimb ischemia-reperfusion in mice, improving perfusion, motor performance, and contractile function while reducing TNF-α and IL-6. It increased LC3-II/I ratio and decreased p62 and phosphorylated mTOR, effects partially abrogated by chloroquine, indicating autophagy modulation involvement.

papers.title: Prognostic value of melatonin-related signature genes in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.summary: Building a melatonin-related gene signature risk model for lung adenocarcinoma from TCGA and validated in GSE31210, eight model genes were selected via Cox regression. The model showed good predictive performance, with ALG3 and FRY significantly related to immune cells and immune checkpoints and E2F1 negatively associated with FRY.

papers.title: Therapeutic effects of Rosmarinus officinalis against methotrexate-induced submandibular salivary gland injury in male albino rats.
papers.summary: Rosmarinus officinalis methanolic extract (200 mg/kg, 10 days) attenuated methotrexate-induced submandibular salivary gland injury in rats, preserving glandular architecture, elevating GSH and NRF2 expression, and reducing caspase-3 immunoreactivity, indicating antioxidant and anti-apoptotic protection against chemotherapy-induced tissue damage.

papers.title: Identification and characterization of a gene conferring stress resistance in Escherichia coli and cyanobacteria.
papers.summary: Screening cyanobacterial genes in E. coli identified PCSYN14890, specific to cyanobacteria, whose expression accelerated growth and stress resistance in E. coli and Synechococcus. Structural characterization showed monomeric/dimeric β-sheet-rich protein, but it failed to prevent GAPDH thermal aggregation, ruling out general molecular chaperone function.

papers.title: Type I interferons modulate autophagy to shape gemcitabine response in pancreatic cancer cells.
papers.summary: Type I interferons differentially modulate autophagy in pancreatic cancer: IFNα2b promoted autophagic flux and reduced gemcitabine-induced cell death (cytoprotective), while IFNβ1a reduced autophagosome formation and enhanced cell death. Both induced STAT1 phosphorylation, suggesting IFNβ1a as a potential chemosensitizing agent for PDAC.

papers.title: Metallotoxicity-driven oxidative perturbations in spinal cord injury: Unraveling the pathophysiological nexus between metal-induced redox imbalance and disease severity: A correlational and multivariate analysis.
papers.summary: In 105 spinal cord injury patients versus matched controls, SCI showed elevated lipid peroxidation, protein carbonyls, nitric oxide, IL-6, and TNF-α with reduced catalase, glutathione peroxidase/reductase, and vitamins A/C/E, alongside altered metal homeostasis—linking metallotoxicity-driven redox imbalance to disease severity.

papers.title: Stage-specific elevation of MPO and NE mRNA expression in diabetic kidney disease and their independent associations with albuminuria.
papers.summary: In 70 type 2 diabetes patients, MPO and neutrophil elastase mRNA in peripheral blood leukocytes were selectively elevated in severe (A3) diabetic kidney disease versus A1/A2, correlated positively with urine albumin and ACR, and independently associated with albuminuria on multivariable regression, indicating enhanced neutrophil activation in advanced DKD.
